title: A Choir for the Harvest
premise: Oscar Sterling returns to her grandmother's house to bury her twin sister Odette, only to find the family photographs have changed: every image now shows an extra chair, and the townspeople of Hollow Creek greet her as 'Odette.' The town's founding families made a bargain in 1974, trading a child to something in the orchard for a generation of impossible harvests, and the debt has come due again. As Oscar investigates, she learns her grandmother substituted one twin for another that year, sparing Oscar and condemning a girl no one remembers. To end it, Oscar must return what was taken—herself—to the orchard, but she chooses instead to break the bargain by naming the forgotten child aloud, unmaking the town's prosperity and freeing both the living and the taken.
about_author: August Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing county records in rural Georgia, where he collected the funeral notices and land deeds that seed his fiction. He writes horror about inheritance—the things families keep, and the things that keep families.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She arrives in Hollow Creek for Odette's funeral and finds the headstone already weathered, as if buried years ago. The minister calls her Odette. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Forty-One Chairs
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At grandma's house she counts chairs in old photographs; every picture since 1974 holds one extra, empty seat facing the camera. Emotional beat: rational mind cracking against evidence.

chapters.title: Condolences from Strangers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Townspeople mourn Odette but speak to Oscar in half-finished sentences, correcting themselves mid-name. Her aunt Ruth begs her to leave before the harvest moon. Emotional beat: isolation.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept Locked
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She finds a locked root cellar and inside, forty jars of preserves labeled with names she doesn't recognize—one per year since 1974. Emotional beat: creeping understanding.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Aunt Ruth begins telling Oscar about the summer of '74 but stops when headlights sweep the drive. Someone has been watching the house. Emotional beat: terror beneath loyalty.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Night
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Drawn by singing, Oscar walks the orchard rows and hears a voice identical to her own answering hers. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Founding Families
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the historical society she finds a ledger: seven families, one signature each, dated October 1974, promising 'a tithe for the yield.' Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Odette's Room
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Odette's bedroom is preserved exactly, dust undisturbed for decades—as if no one ever lived there. A diary's pages are blank except the last: 'She took my name.' Emotional beat: grief inverted.

chapters.title: The Man Who Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Elias Vann's POV. The oldest townsperson tries to recall 1974 and experiences nosebleeds and missing hours; his memories return as dreams of standing in orchard rows, counting children. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing.

chapters.title: Half a Twin
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar discovers records of triplets born in 1961—herself, Odette, and a third girl whose name appears nowhere else. Emotional beat: identity destabilized.

chapters.title: The Harvest Festival Flyer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. This year's festival poster lists her as grand marshal, printed weeks before Odette died. Emotional beat: realization she was always the intended payment.

chapters.title: Ruth Breaks
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth confesses: in 1974 grandma was supposed to give Oscar, but gave the third triplet instead, and the orchard accepted the substitution—for fifty years. Now it wants the original. Emotional beat: shame and love entangled.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Hunting the erased sister's name through baptismal records, Oscar finds it scratched out in every document—but the scratches are fresh. Something is still erasing. Emotional beat: urgency.

chapters.title: Neighbors with Lanterns
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Founding-family descendants surround the house at night, politely insisting she attend a 'reconciliation dinner.' Their kindness is worse than menace. Emotional beat: claustrophobia.

chapters.title: The Reconciliation Dinner
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Seven families seat her at the head of a table set for eight; the eighth chair fills with shadow as they eat. They toast 'the fiftieth yield.' Emotional beat: dread dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Elias's Dream
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias dreams the full night of 1974: the chanting, the child walking into the trees, and grandma's face as she lied to the circle. He wakes knowing the third girl's name—and forgets it by breakfast. Emotional beat: torment.

chapters.title: Photographs That Move
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The extra chair in the photos is no longer empty; a blurred figure sits in it, clearer each day, wearing Oscar's clothes. Emotional beat: horror of being replaced.

chapters.title: The Preserves
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar opens one jar: inside, not fruit but a folded paper bearing a name and a date—next year's label reads OSCAR STERLING. Emotional beat: countdown begins.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar flees toward the county line but the road loops back to Hollow Creek no matter which direction she drives. The town will not release her. Emotional beat: panic and entrapment.

chapters.title: What Odette Knew
chapters.summary: Odette's diary, reconstructed (Oscar reading). Before her death Odette had learned the truth and tried to offer herself in Oscar's place; the orchard refused a substitute twice-used. Emotional beat: devastating love.

chapters.title: The Church Basement
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Beneath the church, Oscar finds the original covenant: seven signatures, one blank line reserved for 'the mother,' signed in grandma's hand. Emotional beat: betrayal made physical.

chapters.title: Grandma Wakes
chapters.summary: Grandma's POV. Senile for years, grandma surfaces lucid for one hour, tells Oscar the third girl's name—Adaeze—and warns: 'Names are doors. Say hers before they say yours.' Emotional beat: desperate transmission.

chapters.title: They Take Grandma's Voice
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. By morning grandma cannot speak; her mouth moves around silence. The town's price for the slip is collected immediately. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness.

chapters.title: Adaeze
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Speaking the name aloud, Oscar feels the house shift; the extra chair in the newest photograph stands empty, its occupant standing behind her in the frame. Emotional beat: awe and terror.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Rows
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV (first time). Fifty years in the orchard as 'the yield,' Adaeze has kept herself whole by refusing to answer when called. Oscar's speaking her name gives her a self again. Emotional beat: resurrection of identity.

chapters.title: The Bargain's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar rereads the covenant and finds the escape clause the founders ignored: the debt ends if the taken is named and willingly released by all seven bloodlines. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Seven Doors
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar spends days petitioning each founding family; most refuse, terrified of losing the harvests that made them rich. One, the Vanns, sign at once. Emotional beat: grinding resistance.

chapters.title: Elias Signs, and Pays
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. After signing, Elias's decades of stolen memory flood back at once; he collapses under the weight of everything the town made him forget. Emotional beat: costly redemption.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With four signatures still missing and the moon nearly full, the orchard begins taking prematurely—livestock first, then the pastor's son. Emotional beat: escalating stakes.

chapters.title: Ruth's Choice
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth holds a fifth signature—her own bloodline—but hesitates, because releasing the bargain means admitting grandma's crime publicly. She signs. Emotional beat: loyalty finally bending toward truth.

chapters.title: The Empty Pews
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar confronts the remaining families at Sunday service; the congregation's faces blur identically, the town itself resisting through them. Two more sign out of fear, not conscience. Emotional beat: moral compromise.

chapters.title: One Signature Short
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The last holdout is the Halloway matriarch, whose fortune depends on the yield. She offers Oscar a deal: take Adaeze's place willingly and her family prospers forever. Emotional beat: temptation.

chapters.title: What Oscar Almost Did
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Standing in the orchard at dusk, ready to trade herself, Oscar hears Adaeze singing—not a lure but a lullaby, the one their mother sang to three girls. She turns back. Emotional beat: the darkest hour passed.

chapters.title: The Halloway Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar finds proof the Halloways skimmed from every other family's share for fifty years; armed with it, she forces the final signature. Emotional beat: power turned against corruption.

chapters.title: All Seven
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At midnight on the harvest moon, seven bloodlines stand at the orchard's edge and speak Adaeze's name together, releasing her. The trees go silent. Emotional beat: trembling triumph.

chapters.title: The Orchard Gives Back
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Walking out of the rows, Adaeze ages into her true fifty-some years between one step and the next, carrying the faces of every season inside her. Emotional beat: homecoming after erasure.

chapters.title: The Yield Fails
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The fields brown overnight; the town's wealth rots on the vine. Some curse Oscar; others weep with relief. Emotional beat: liberation's price made visible.

chapters.title: Three Names on a Stone
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar replaces Odette's headstone with one bearing three names: Odette, Adaeze, and the words 'and the one who was spared.' She finally grieves properly. Emotional beat: mourning completed.

chapters.title: The Last Photograph
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Packing up grandma's house, Oscar takes one final photo of the kitchen table: three chairs, occupied by three sisters' memories, no extras. Emotional beat: quiet restoration.

chapters.title: Leaving Hollow Creek
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar drives out at dawn and this time the road lets her go. In the rearview, the orchard is just trees. But in her pocket, a jar labeled with tomorrow's date sits empty—waiting to be filled with something chosen, not owed. Emotional beat: hard-won freedom, vigilantly kept.
